title: Secret redaction is enabled in every Hermes home
summary: Secret values are redacted before they reach model-visible context or stored transcripts.

protected.failure: Secret values are printed into transcripts, reports or model context where they can be exfiltrated or committed.

rationale: Redaction is a cheap, high-leverage default: it reduces accidental disclosure in every downstream artifact without changing any credential. It reduces accidental disclosure; it does not prevent exfiltration by a malicious process with the same access, and the registry never treats it as containment.

variants.description: Enable the deployment's secret-redaction setting in every home of the deployment.
Enable redaction and additionally sweep configuration and report files for literal credential shapes before any mirror or publication.

verification.method: Read the resolved secret-redaction setting back per home and confirm the effective value in each, including named profiles that may inherit built-in defaults.
verification.evidence: Per-home read-back of the setting name and effective value only.

rollback.method: Restore the previous setting value; redaction itself has no state beyond configuration.

failure_modes: A named profile inherits a permissive built-in default instead of the intended value.
Redaction is read as enabled from one home and wrongly assumed for every other home.

hermes_versions.notes: Synthetic seed control: the range is an illustrative placeholder for the example registry, not a verified compatibility claim.
